trap-nonspeakable.notes: SUBSTANTIVE FINDING, not fixable inline: 'The Markov trace of the Garside element yields a non-torus braid, contributing a positive hyperbolic JSJ piece.' I COMPUTED THE CLOSURE. The Garside element of B_3 is sigma_1 sigma_2 sigma_1; cyclic permutation (closure-preserving) gives sigma_1 sigma_1 sigma_2 = sigma_1^2 sigma_2, and sigma_2 occurs exactly once with sigma_1^2 in B_2, so Markov destabilisation gives closure_{B_3}(sigma_1^2 sigma_2) = closure_{B_2}(sigma_1^2) = the (2,2) torus link = THE HOPF LINK. Component count confirms independently: the induced permutation (12)(23)(12) = (13) has cycle type (2,1), so 2 components. The Hopf link is a TORUS link with hyperbolic volume ZERO — so the Garside closure is neither non-torus nor a positive-volume hyperbolic piece. This is the documented recurring braid-closure error class, here with the label inverted. THE SAME CLAIM APPEARS IN six-canonical-knot-operators-context.md ('The Garside trajectory crosses between Heegaard tori, yielding a hyperbolic piece with positive volume') and both need correcting together. The 3-cycle half of the sentence IS CORRECT: closure_{B_3}(sigma_1 sigma_2) destabilises to closure_{B_2}(sigma_1) = the unknot, volume 0.
